Assistant: Understood — and your follow-up changes the core data model: **no `limit`, and the filter can return multiple events**, so this is a multi-result mechanism, not a single-pointer reduction. That matches what the design's own §3.5 flagged as the "future extension" via `DynamicTargetProjection` — you want that generality from day one. I'll build it that way: an AD URL resolves to `{filter, relays}` → a live query yielding 0..N events → embed renders each / search shows a result set.

I have enough grounding on the security-critical and ProtocolCommand seams. Let me set up an isolated worktree and dispatch the implementation.

Assistant: Both examples locked in: `golf.com/highlights` → many `kind:20` images, `trellis.rs/legible` → one `kind:30023`. So **multi-result is first-class**: a URL resolves to a live `{filter, relays}` query yielding 0..N events, and both the embed renderer (gallery/list of cards) and search results must render the whole set — exactly the `DynamicTargetProjection` collection pattern, never a single-pointer reduction, never a `limit`. [...] - **App-injected `AdResolutionPolicy`** (Never / Always / FollowsOnly / WebOfTrust) — no framework default; the app picks at its composition root, like content-component registration.
- **Multi-result first-class, no `limit`** — resolves to a live `{filter, relays}` collection query. `golf.com/highlights` → gallery of kind:20 images; `trellis.rs/legible` → one kind:30023 article; both through the same `DynamicTargetProjection` collection path. [...] 3. The well-known returns **all** path entries regardless of `?ad=` — so the resolver must select the key matching our path, not blindly take the first.
 [...] | **Caching** | URL-keyed, in-memory, LRU cache. ~6h TTL on success, ~24h on failure (the common case), doubling as a fetch debounce. |
